records.description: Taking both greatly increases the risk of serious bleeding.
NSAIDs increase bleeding risk and may irritate the stomach lining while on warfarin.
Ciprofloxacin can raise warfarin levels and INR, increasing bleeding risk.
Metronidazole strongly increases the effect of warfarin; INR can rise sharply.
Azithromycin may increase INR in some patients; closer INR monitoring may be needed.
Regular or high-dose paracetamol can raise INR; occasional use is generally considered lower risk.
Omeprazole can reduce activation of clopidogrel and lower its antiplatelet effect.
Esomeprazole may reduce the antiplatelet effect of clopidogrel.
Combined antiplatelet therapy increases bleeding risk; often prescribed together on purpose under supervision.
Ibuprofen may reduce the heart-protective effect of low-dose aspirin and adds to stomach bleeding risk.
NSAIDs can reduce the blood-pressure-lowering effect of losartan and may affect kidney function.
Ciprofloxacin can cause unpredictable changes in blood sugar in people taking diabetes medicines.
Ciprofloxacin may increase the blood-sugar-lowering effect of gliclazide, risking hypoglycaemia.
Rare reports of muscle problems when combined; report unexplained muscle pain.
Amlodipine may slightly increase atorvastatin levels; usually not clinically significant.
